projects.title: Anguilla Summer 2026 — June 26–30 Trip Guide
projects.topic: Things to do in Anguilla over Friday June 26 – Tuesday June 30, 2026 for a traveler based at Zemi Beach House (Shoal Bay East) with a rental car: live music and nightlife, food, must-see beaches, and attractions, sequenced into a practical day-by-day itinerary.
projects.summary: A four-day, itinerary-ready guide to Anguilla (Jun 26–30, 2026) from a base at Zemi Beach House, timed to the island's weekly rhythm — Dune Preserve music (closed Mondays), Elvis' Saturday DJ night, Scilly Cay on Sunday — plus top beaches, restaurants, and east-end attractions, with car/driving tips.
key_claims: The trip dates fall Fri Jun 26 / Sat 27 / Sun 28 / Mon 29 / Tue 30, 2026, and Anguilla's nightlife runs on a weekly schedule — sequence the itinerary to the day of week.
Zemi Beach House sits on Shoal Bay East (East End) with five restaurants and a 300-year-old Thai spa house on property.
The Dune Preserve (Bankie Banx) on Rendezvous Bay is the island's top music venue: live music Fri/Sat and Sunday afternoons, Friday BBQ — but it is CLOSED on Mondays.
Elvis' Beach Bar (Sandy Ground) runs DJ Kue on Saturday nights and a Sunday beach BBQ.
Scilly Cay off Island Harbour is open Wed/Thu/Sun (~11–3:30) with grilled crayfish and live Sunday music — Sunday Jun 28 is the window; flag down the free ferry from the dock.
Must-see beaches: Shoal Bay East (at the resort), Rendezvous Bay, Meads Bay, Little Bay, Sandy Island, Shoal Bay West.
Top dining: Blanchards and Veya (fine dining), Hibernia, Tasty's and Smokey's (local), plus beach bars; book the big names ahead in low-season late June.
Driving is on the left; a ~US$25 temporary permit is arranged by the rental company; roads are flat, low-traffic, 30 mph limit.

projects.title: Azure Workspaces
projects.topic: How an Azure engagement boundary is built: Tenant -> Subscription -> Resource Groups -> Workspace, and how agents operate inside it
projects.summary: Walks the Azure hierarchy (Entra tenant, subscription, resource groups, regions) and builds the Workspace as a data boundary around an engagement, with agents operating safely inside it.
key_claims: The Azure chain is Tenant -> Subscription -> Resource Group -> Workspace boundary.
A Microsoft Entra ID tenant is the organization identity boundary.
A subscription is a billing and access container; a tenant can hold many.
Resource groups are lifecycle buckets of resources, each pinned to a real region/data center.
A Workspace is a data boundary around the resource groups of one engagement and can grow over time.
A single KPMG engagement number ties the whole boundary to governance.
Agents operate only inside the Workspace boundary, feeding good changes to a golden instance.

projects.title: Enterprise LLM Token Economics (Tokenomics)
projects.topic: Enterprise LLM token economics (tokenomics): the basic concept, recent news stories of runaway-cost failures, and state-of-the-art practices for managing token spend across an organization
projects.summary: Explains how LLMs are billed by the token (input vs. output, the re-billed context window), surveys 2025-2026 news of runaway token costs (agent loops burning tens of thousands of dollars, annual AI budgets gone in a quarter), and lays out the state-of-the-art FinOps-for-AI playbook: token-level attribution, pre-execution budget enforcement, an LLM gateway with caching/routing, and governance.
key_claims: LLMs are billed by the token (~4 chars each); input and output are priced separately and output typically costs 2-4x more than input.
The context window is re-sent and re-billed on every call, so long system prompts and growing history compound cost.
Agentic workflows use an estimated 5-30x the tokens of a single chat query, and pilot per-query economics do not predict production bills.
Vendor-reported failure cases include a 4-agent loop running ~11 days for ~$47,000 and enterprises exhausting an annual AI budget within a quarter.
The core lesson of the failures: alerting is not enforcement -- you need pre-execution budget caps, not just dashboards.
The maturing response is FinOps for AI: token-level cost attribution to teams/features/workflows for unit economics.
An LLM gateway is the control plane -- centralizing budget enforcement, prompt/semantic caching, model routing, and metering.
Engineering levers stack: prompt caching (~90% off cached input), batch APIs (~50% off), and model routing (reported 40-70% savings).
Governance closes the loop with enforced per-team budgets, showback/chargeback, and forecasting on unit economics.
